summary: Stage 1 of the clean 10k baseline is accepted as a serial single-worker, one-GPU measurement with the stated caveats. All six native reports (byte copies in build/baseline10k-evidence) show status pass, 10000 delivered events, 1000 warmup + 9000 steady, 1500 callbacks (1000x7, 500x6), zero admission drains, 512 KiB target, 4 GiB budget, identical runtime/code/calibration hashes, same host/job, and strictly increasing monotonic sample times across the s1-r1,s2-r1,s1-r2,s2-r2,s1-r3,s2-r3 order. The warmed-window rates, medians (257.2539490 / 283.5848556), ratio 1.10235375, whole-iteration medians (255.2739519 / 279.2474533) and sample stdevs were independently recomputed from the report seconds and match summary.json and the README table. The six JSON blocks in the normalized job stdout match the window figures in the report copies, giving an independent native cross-check on those numbers even though hashes could not be verified. callbacks.csv has 9000 rows (6x1500), 900 warmup rows (6x150 callbacks = exactly 1000 events), and alternating stream handles for two-stream cases consistent with the 5000/5000 bank split. summarize.py checks are substantive (bin reconstruction from callback order, warmup/event conservation, rate re-derivation, identity equality, execution order), and the fixture receipt it reads exists with matching root and generation_sha256. Claim strength in README/plan is appropriately hedged: no causal speedup, no comparison with the prior 1k runs, outlier retained, GPU exclusivity not asserted. Plan/README edits only link the completed stage and name batch tuning/short profiling as next; this review does not authorize those stages. Two non-blocking findings: the build/ evidence lacks the copy-index.json the scope describes, so review copies are not formally bound to the hash-bound originals; and README does not disclose the post-campaign snapshot's 97% utilization reading alongside the pre-campaign 100%/6373 MiB disclosure.

Verified monotonic_seconds strictly increase across cases in the documented execution order (s1-r1 end 3132851.06 < s2-r1 start 3132856.67 < ... < s2-r3)

Verified all six reports carry identical runtime, runtime_files, code_sha256, calibration ids/hashes, fixture_check, host sdfampere011, job 43859846; source-verification.json hashes match report code_sha256 and launch-sha256.txt (27 files incl. runner, test_preparation.py, summarize.py, test_summary.py)
